The axis is "num" — certificate number.

Register: "R107/1997-FR2-2005.01"
Document: "R 107/1997 – FR2 – 05.01"

These are clearly the same certificate number with formatting differences:
- Register: R107/1997-FR2-2005.01
- Document: R 107/1997 – FR2 – 05.01

Breaking down:
- "R107" vs "R 107" — spacing difference
- "1997-FR2-2005.01" vs "1997 – FR2 – 05.01" — the document uses "05.01" which is shorthand for "2005.01" (year 2005, certificate 01). The register uses full year "2005.01". The en-dash vs hyphen is formatting.

The rule: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value: "R107/1997-FR2-2005.01" (register canonical form).

Why: The document's number uses spacing, en-dashes, and abbreviated year ("05.01" vs "2005.01") but unambiguously denotes the same certificate; keep register canonical form.
